nc_upper_tier_4.blurb: A small trad cliff above the Blue Ridge Parkway, tucked up the slope from the main face of Ship Rock near the Linn Cove Viaduct. The thirteen lines run from 5.7 up to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.9 range and a handful of 5.11s for stronger leaders. The quartzite is solid, and a modest rack of nuts and cams up to about a number 2 is all most lines ask for. Climbs are short but exposed, and the ledge setting gives wide views over the Blue Ridge. Expect a scramble through gullies and a rock tunnel to reach the base, so it suits climbers comfortable on rough ground.
nc_upper_tier_4.parking_note: Leave the car in the Rough Ridge lot on the Blue Ridge Parkway, close to milepost 303, then walk south along the Parkway toward the Linn Cove Viaduct.

nc_black_mountain_range_alpine.blurb: Remote winter terrain in the Black Mountains of Yancey County, reached by forest roads off Highway 80 south of Micaville. The routes are mostly frozen waterfalls and snow gullies, many several pitches and hundreds of feet long, with grades mainly from WI2 to WI4 and WI3 the most common. One easy scramble and a single boulder problem round out the list. Days here are committing: expect a long bushwhack in, a long walk out, and the need for route-finding and backup navigation. Conditions depend on a cold, snowy spell, so it is a destination for experienced parties rather than a quick roadside ice fix.

nc_upper_hawksbill.blurb: The highest of three walls on Hawksbill Mountain in Linville Gorge, a mountain with both hard trad and sport climbing. This wall has twelve routes, mostly sport with a few trad lines, and most of them sit at 5.12 and 5.13 with only a few easier lines in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. That makes it a place for strong climbers rather than beginners. A climbers' trail splits off the summit path from the trailhead to reach it, and the middle wall lies a few hundred yards farther along the same trail.
